solution: 5 orbitals × 2 electrons = 10.

solution: l determines the subshell type: s, p, d, f.

solution: No two electrons in an atom can have the same set of all four quantum numbers.

q: Across a period, atomic radius generally:
solution: Increasing nuclear charge pulls electrons closer.

q: Which has the largest atomic radius?
solution: Radius increases down the group.

q: Why does ionisation energy decrease down a group?
solution: The outer electron is farther from the nucleus and shielded by more inner shells, so it is easier to remove.

q: Why does electronegativity increase across a period?
solution: Effective nuclear charge increases while atomic size decreases, so atoms attract bonding electrons more strongly.

solution: Loss of electrons and reduced repulsion contract the ion.

solution: Helium's tightly held 1s electrons need the most energy to remove.

q: Why is the second ionisation energy of sodium much greater than the first?
solution: Removing a second electron from a stable noble-gas configuration requires far more energy.

solution: Four bonding pairs arrange tetrahedrally.

q: Lone pair–lone pair repulsion is:
solution: Lone pairs occupy more space near the central atom.

solution: Boron has three bonding pairs and no lone pairs, so they spread 120° apart.

q: Why is the bond angle in water less than in ammonia?
solution: Water has two lone pairs versus one in ammonia, so lone-pair repulsion compresses the angle more.

solution: Molecules are forced close together, so their finite volume and intermolecular attractions become significant.

solution: Enthalpy is a state function, so the route does not matter.

solution: Energy can be exchanged as heat or work, but the total energy of the universe is conserved: ΔU = q + w.

q: A spontaneous reaction has:
solution: Negative Gibbs energy means spontaneity.

q: Entropy is a measure of:
solution: Higher disorder means higher entropy.

q: Why is the combustion of fuels spontaneous even though it releases heat?
solution: It is strongly exothermic and increases entropy of the surroundings, giving ΔG < 0.

solution: Reactivity increases down the group.

solution: Magnesium gives a bright white light.

q: Why are alkali metals stored in kerosene?
solution: They react rapidly with air and moisture, so kerosene keeps them dry and unreactive.

q: Caustic soda is:

solution: Slaked lime forms a white protective layer.

solution: Sodium maintains fluid balance, nerve impulses and muscle contraction.

solution: Diamond's rigid covalent network makes it hardest.

solution: Each carbon has a delocalised electron that is free to move along the layers.

solution: They have filled outer shells with very high ionisation energies and no tendency to gain electrons.

solution: Its delocalised π system is stable, so it does not undergo addition like alkenes.

solution: Free-radical substitution replaces a hydrogen.

solution: Unsaturated hydrocarbons add bromine and decolourise the solution.

solution: They are highly reduced and release a lot of heat on complete combustion.

solution: Its delocalised π electrons are spread over the ring, lowering the energy of the molecule.

solution: Sunlight drives the reactions that produce ozone and other oxidants.

solution: Algal blooms die and decomposition uses up oxygen.

solution: Designing chemical products and processes that reduce or eliminate hazardous substances.
